item.title: WATCH- Virat Kohli gets flocked by legion of fans as he lands in Baroda for first IND v NZ 2026 ODI
item.description: Ace India batter Virat Kohli has arrived in Baroda along with other members of the Indian cricket team. India will play the first of the three ODIs against New Zealand at the Kotambi Stadium, Vadodara, on January 11. New Zealand will then play the next two ODIs on January 14 in Rajkot and January 18 in Indore. The two teams will then clash in five T20Is as well, which will be played from January 21 to 31. item.title: WATCH- Vaibhav Sooryavanshi's ‘Pushpa’ celebration after hitting 63-ball ton in 3rd IND U19 v SA U19 one-dayer
item.description: Captain of the India U19 team that is on tour of South Africa, Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, has been in good form in the 50-over format in recent matches. item.title: “We are adamant in this position,” Bangladesh reiterate stand of not wanting to play T20 World Cup 2026 matches in India
item.description: The Bangladesh Cricket Board (BCB) top officials on Wednesday (January 7) conducted a high-level meeting regarding their stand of not playing T20 World Cup 2026 fixtures in India. In the meeting, it was decided that BCB will try to persuade the International Cricket Council (ICC) to relocate their T20 World Cup matches to Sri Lanka. item.title: “These things shouldn’t be in our game”: Jason Holder expresses sadness over India-Pakistan beef
item.description: West Indies all-rounder Jason Holder has expressed his sadness over the ongoing India-Pakistan divide, saying that it should not be allowed to overshadow the game. During the Asia Cup 2025 in the UAE, the Suryakumar Yadav-led Indian side refrained from shaking hands with their Pakistani counterparts as the games were played amidst heightened tensions between two nations following the Pahalgam terror attack and retaliatory Operation Sindoor. item.title: “I’m not blaming Bangladesh”: Moeen Ali voices against growing politics in cricket after Mustafizur Rahman’s IPL axing
item.description: Kolkata Knight Riders (KKR) on Saturday (January 3) released Mustafizur Rahman from their Indian Premier League (IPL) 2026 roster after receiving BCCI’s directive. Mustafizur, the only Bangladeshi representative in the upcoming IPL season, was signed by KKR for Rs 9.2 crore in the mini-auction last month. item.description: Asif Nazrul, Bangladesh's Youth and Sports Advisor, has publicly questioned whether the International Cricket Council (ICC) truly understands the seriousness of the situation pertaining to the national team's participation in the 2026 T20 World Cup matches that are set to take place in India. item.title: “Don't fight it”- Shreyanka Patil reveals advice from Jasprit Bumrah during her recovery from various injuries
item.description: India all-rounder Shreyanka Patil will be returning to competitive cricket after a 14-month injury layoff when she features for the Royal Challengers Bengaluru women’s team (RCB) in the upcoming Women’s Premier League (WPL 2026). item.title: “Things need to change”: Michael Vaughan wants England to ditch high-risk 'Bazball' approach after Ashes 2025-26 debacle
item.description: England must finally move away from their high-risk 'Bazball' approach and return to Test cricket basics after their dismal Ashes 2025-26 campaign, reckons former captain Michael Vaughan. The Ben Stokes-led side arrived Down Under with a lot of expectations, but ended up conceding the urn in just 11 days -- the joint-second quickest in more than a century. item.title: “Slap in the face came at 20-21,” Stuart Broad reflects on Yuvraj Singh’s 6 sixes against him during T20 World Cup 2007
item.description: India’s T20 World Cup 2007 fixture against England is known for Yuvraj Singh’s heroics as he created history by hitting Stuart Broad for 6 sixes in an over, becoming the first-ever batter to achieve the feat in the shortest format. Yuvraj slammed a jaw-dropping 14-ball 58 which proved to be the difference between the two sides as India won the match by 18 runs. item.title: Tilak Varma undergoes surgery for testicular torsion; faces race against time to be fit for T20 World Cup 2026
item.description: India’s middle-order batter Tilak Varma has suffered an abdominal injury, which could sideline him for three to four weeks. The development comes with less than a month remaining for the T20 World Cup 2026, slated to be held in India and Sri Lanka from February 7 to March 8. While the southpaw is set to miss the upcoming five-T20I series against New Zealand, he faces race against time to be fit for the global showpiece.
